'''Virander Singh Chauhan''' is an Indian scientist<ref name="Profile on Vidwan Database">{{cite web | url=http://vidwan.inflibnet.ac.in/searchr.php?id=15361 | title=Profile on Vidwan Database | publisher=Vidwan Database | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> and a [[Rhodes Scholar]]<ref name="The Rhodes Trust">{{cite web | url=http://www.rhodeshouse.ox.ac.uk/news-and-events/recent-appointments-of-rhodes-scholars/virander-singh-chauhan-india-st-catherines-1974 | title=The Rhodes Trust | publisher=The Rhodes Trust | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> working in the fields of [[genetic engineering]] and [[biotechnology]]. He is known for his contributions to the development of a [[recombinant vaccine]] for [[malaria]].<ref name="Biotech Park">{{cite web | url=http://www.biotechpark.org.in/Annaul_day/Biodata%20of%20Dr.%20CHauhan.pdf | title=Biotech Park | publisher=Biotech Park | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref><ref name="INSA Profile">{{cite web | url=http://insaindia.org/detail.php?id=n99-1246 | title=INSA Profile | publisher=INSA | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref><ref name="ICGEB">{{cite web | url=http://www.icgeb.org/virander-chauhan.html | title=ICGEB | publisher=ICGEB | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> and for synthetic structural peptides with biological functions. He was honored by the [[Government of India]] in 2012 with the fourth highest Indian civilian award of [[Padma Shri]].<ref name="Padma Shri">{{cite web | url=http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | title=Padma Shri | publisher=Padma Shri | date=2014 | access-date=November 11, 2014 | archive-date=October 15, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015193758/http://mha.nic.in/sites/upload_files/mha/files/LST-PDAWD-2013.pdf | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="TOI Padma">{{cite web | url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/15-Delhiites-grace-Padma-list-tricolour-skier-on-top-of-world/articleshow/11634406.cms?referral=PM | title=TOI Padma | publisher=TOI Padma | date=26 January 2012 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> He is the present Chancellor of the [https://www.gitam.edu/ Gandhi Institute of Technology and Management].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://telanganatoday.com/gitam-appoints-dr-virander-singh-as-new-chancellor | title=GITAM appoints Dr Virander Singh as new Chancellor | date=6 August 2021 }}</ref>

==Biography==
Virander Singh Chauhan, born on 3 March 1950,<ref name="Biotech Park" /> graduated in Chemistry (BSc) from the [[University of Delhi]] in 1969 and secured his post graduation (MSc) from the same university in 1971.<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="INSA Profile" /><ref name="ICGEB" /> His career started as the faculty member of Chemistry at the [[St. Stephen's College, Delhi|St. Stephen's College]], Delhi and continued his research at Delhi University.<ref name="Qatar Foundation">{{cite web | url=http://www.qf-qfirst.info/bio/Dr_Virander_Singh_Chauhan.html | title=Qatar Foundation | publisher=Qatar Foundation | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> In 1974, he obtained a Ph.D., after which he moved to [[Oxford University]], on temporary leave from the college, on a Rhodes Scholarship where he stayed till 1977.<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="INSA Profile" /><ref name="ICGEB" /> At Oxford he obtained his D.Phil. in chemistry<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Virander Chauhan |url=https://www.etiservices.org/drviranderchauhan |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=ETI |language=en}}</ref> in 1977.On his return from  Oxford, he resumed his duties at St. Stephen's College where he worked till 1979.<ref name="Biotech Park" /> In between, he had a brief stay of one year as a post doctoral fellow at the [[University of Georgia]] during 1977-78.<ref name="INSA Profile" /><ref name="ICGEB" /><ref name="Qatar Foundation" />

In 1979, Chauhan joined the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]] as an Assistant Professor and returned to Delhi University in 1982 as the Reader of the Department of Chemistry.<ref name="ICGEB" /> In 1986, he was promoted as the Professor and worked there till 1988.<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="INSA Profile" /><ref name="ICGEB" /><ref name="Qatar Foundation" /> Resigning from the university, Chauhan joined the [[International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology]] (ICGEB), a non profit research organization under the aegis of [[United Nations Industrial Development Organization]]<ref name="ICGEB Home">{{cite web | url=http://www.icgeb.org/about-the-centre.html | title=ICGEB Home | publisher=ICGEB Home | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> as senior scientist and was entrusted the leadership of the workgroup involved in the research on Malaria. In 1998, he was appointed as the Director of the institute,<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="INSA Profile" /> a post he held till 2014.<ref name="ICGEB" />[5] Besides academic achievements Chauhan was also an outstanding athlete who represented Delhi University and Oxford University in Athletics and Cross-Country running. Chauhan continued his research at ICGEB as a DBT distinguished biotechnology professor fellow, JC Bose fellow and Arturo Falaschi Fellow till the end of 2022.<ref name="Virander S. Chauhan">{{Cite web |date=2020-06-16 |title=Virander S. Chauhan |url=https://www.icgeb.org/virander-s-chauhan/ |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=ICGEB |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Positions==
Virander Chauhan was the secretary of the Indian arm of [[Rhodes Scholarships]] UK and is a member of the selection committees of  such as Inlaks, Felix and Dr. Manmohan Singh scholarships.<ref name="Biotech Park" /> Chauhan has been on the selection committees for the last 42 years without a break.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AWARDS AND HONOURS - YoungBites |url=http://youngbites.com/newsdet.aspx?q=289293 |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=youngbites.com}}</ref> A former president of the Society of Biological Chemists during 2009-2011, Chauhan is an elected member (1992) of all the three National Academies of Sciences including the [[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA), [[National Academy of Sciences, India|National Academy of Sciences]] (NASI), and [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (IAS)<ref name="Virander S. Chauhan"/> as well as [[Guha Research Conference]] and [[The World Academy of Sciences]] TWAS.<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="INSA Profile" /><ref name="Qatar Foundation" /> He has served as the president of Indian Peptide Society and as a member of scientific institutions such as [[New York Academy of Sciences]], American Society of Microbiology, Indian Biophysical Society and Indian Immunology Society.<ref name="INSA Profile" /> [4] Chauhan was deeply involved in the establishment of several prestigious government funded institutions including Translational Health Science and Technology Institute (THSTI), Regional Centre for Biotechnology (RCB), National Institute of Biomedical Genomics (NIBMG), Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD), National Agri-Food Biotechnology Institute (NABI). He has been the member of the governing council of the MS Swaminathan Research Foundation (MSSRF), the Inter-University Centre for Astronomy and Astrophysics (IUCAA), Chairman of governing board of the L V Prasad Eye Institute (LVPEI),<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.lvpei.org/about-us/board-members |title=Boards Of Management |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=www.lvpei.org}}</ref> the International Clinical Epidemiology Network (INCLEN), the Inter-University Accelerator Centre (IUAC).

He has been a member of the executive councils of [[Jawaharlal Nehru University, Delhi|Jawaharlal Nehru University]], Delhi and the [[Department of Biotechnology]] (DBT) for their Indo-US Vaccine Action Programme.<ref name="INSA Profile" /> He has also been a part of other initiatives by Department of Biotechnology, ''Rotaviral Diarrhoea Vaccine Product Development Project'' and ''Molecular Biophysics and Biochemistry Programme'' and has served as the part-time chairman of ''Bharat Immunologicals and Biologicals Corporation Limited'', a vaccine manufacturing company under DBT.<ref name="INSA Profile" />

Chauhan has been associated with international bodies such as the [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) as the member of the ''Expert Advisory Panel on Vaccines and Biological Standards'', [[International Union of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology]] (IUBMB) and Asia-Pacific International Molecular Biology Network (A-IMBN),<ref name="AIMBN">{{cite web | url=http://www.a-imbn.org/ | title=AIMBN | publisher=AIMBN | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> South Korea, as a member of their ''Technical Research Groups''.<ref name="INSA Profile" /> He has also been a part of the editorial boards of several national and international journals like ''International Journal of Biomedical Science'',<ref name="IJBS">{{cite web | url=http://www.ijbs.org/HomePage.aspx | title=IJBS | publisher=IJBS | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> ''Journal of Biomedicine and Biotechnology'',<ref name="JBB">{{cite web | url=http://www.scimagojr.com/journalsearch.php?q=15850&tip=sid | title=JBB | publisher=Scimagojr | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> [[Journal of Peptide Science]], ''Asian Biotechnology and Development Review'',<ref name="ABDR">{{cite web | url=http://www.scimagojr.com/journalsearch.php?q=14967&tip=sid&clean=0 | title=ABDR | publisher=Scimagojr | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> ''Pakistan Journal of Biological Sciences'',<ref name="PJBS">{{cite web | url=http://www.scimagojr.com/journalsearch.php?q=3900148614&tip=sid&clean=0
 | title=PJBS | publisher=Scimagojr | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> ''Indian Journal for Biochemistry and Biophysics'',<ref name="IJBB">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/journal/0301-1208_Indian_journal_of_biochemistry_biophysics | title=IJBB | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> [[Journal of Molecular Structure]] and ''The Open Vaccine Journal''.<ref name="INSA Profile" /><ref name="TOV">{{cite web | url=https://www.researchgate.net/journal/1875-0354_The_Open_Vaccine_Journal | title=TOV | publisher=TOV | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=INSA :: Indian Fellow Detail |url=https://insaindia.res.in/detail.php?id=N99-1246 |access-date=2023-03-28 |website=insaindia.res.in}}</ref> The Fruiteries of Immunology.

His many other national responsibilities include member of University Grants Commission (UGC)<ref name="Virander S. Chauhan"/> for two terms, Acting Chairman of University Grants Commission (UGC) for one year (2017) as well as the Chairman of the Executive Council of the National Assessment and Accreditation Council<ref name="Virander S. Chauhan"/> (NAAC), Government of India. Chauhan was also the Chairman of the Academic Committee of the 7th pay Commission, Government of India and was responsible for major reforms both at the UGC and NAAC. He is also an independent director of the Higher Education Financing Agency<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-07-28 |title=About Us {{!}} HEFA |url=https://hefa.co.in/about-us/ |access-date=2023-03-28 |language=en-US}}</ref> (HEFA) since its inception. He is also the Chairman of the Governing Council of the Sun Pharma Research Foundation.

==Legacy==
Virander Chauhan was the leader of the workgroup engaged in the development of a vaccine during his early years in the [[International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology]].<ref name="ICGEB" /> His team is known to have developed a [[recombinant vaccine]],<ref name="Qatar Foundation" /> the first time such vaccine developed entirely in India, which is now in its clinical trials stage.<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="INSA Profile" /><ref name="ICGEB" /> His research has also assisted in the understanding of [[artemisinin]] and [[chloroquine]], drugs used in the treatment of Malaria.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pandey|first1=A. V.|last2=Tekwani|first2=B. L.|last3=Singh|first3=R. L.|last4=Chauhan|first4=V. S.|date=1999-07-02|title=Artemisinin, an endoperoxide antimalarial, disrupts the hemoglobin catabolism and heme detoxification systems in malarial parasite|journal=The Journal of Biological Chemistry|volume=274|issue=27|pages=19383–19388|doi=10.1074/jbc.274.27.19383|issn=0021-9258|pmid=10383451|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="ICGEB" /><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pandey|first1=A. V.|last2=Bisht|first2=H.|last3=Babbarwal|first3=V. K.|last4=Srivastava|first4=J.|last5=Pandey|first5=K. C.|last6=Chauhan|first6=V. S.|date=2001-04-15|title=Mechanism of malarial haem detoxification inhibition by chloroquine|journal=The Biochemical Journal|volume=355|issue=Pt 2|pages=333–338|doi=10.1042/0264-6021:3550333|issn=0264-6021|pmc=1221743|pmid=11284719}}</ref> It is also reported to have helped in the development of ''high throughput screens'' for the discovery of drugs for Malaria.<ref name="INSA Profile" /><ref name="ICGEB" /> He has also done research on conformationally defined [[Peptides]], which is of significance for developing antibiotic peptides as well as anti-fibrillizing structures (anti [[amyloids]]) that may help in finding treatment protocols for diseases like [[HIV/AIDS|HIV]] and [[Diabetes mellitus type 2]].<ref name="Biotech Park" /> The work has also led to the formation of [[nanostructures]] to be used as biomolecular delivery agents.<ref name="INSA Profile" /><ref name="ICGEB" />

Virander Singh Chauhan is known to have guided over 50 research students<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="Qatar Foundation" /> and is credited with over 300 research papers, published in peer reviewed  international journals.<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="Qatar Foundation" /> His papers are also featured on known research databases such as [[Microsoft Academic Search]],<ref name="Microsoft Academic Search">{{cite web | url=http://65.54.113.239/PublicationList?srcType=2&desType=2&srcID=18445769&desID=19813534 | title=Microsoft Academic Search | publisher=Microsoft Academic Search | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> PubFacts<ref name="PubFacts">{{cite web | url=http://www.pubfacts.com/author/Virander+Singh+Chauhan | title=PubFacts | publisher=PubFacts | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> and [[Pubget]].<ref name="PubGet">{{cite web | url=http://pubget.com/author/virander-singh-chauhan | title=PubGet | publisher=PubGet | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> He has also delivered keynote addresses at many seminars and conferences,<ref name="Keynote address">{{cite web | url=http://www.niper.ac.in/ISRAM_web/Conference_Programmee_Schedule.pdf | title=Keynote address | publisher=NIPER | date=2014 | access-date=December 11, 2014}}</ref> workshops and convocations at several universities.

==Awards and recognitions==
Virander Chauhan, a Rhodes Scholar of 1974 and a Fellow of the [[Academy of Sciences for the Developing World]] (TWAS),<ref name="INSA Profile" /> received Dr. MOT Iyengar Memorial Award from the [[Indian Council of Medical Research]] (ICMR) in 1995.<ref name="INSA Profile" /> This was followed by [[Ranbaxy]] Research Award in 2001, Om Prakash Bhasin Award in 2002 and [[Indian Council for Medical Research|ICMR]] Basanti Devi Amir Chand Prize in 2003.<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="INSA Profile" /> He is also a recipient of Raj Kristo Dutt Memorial Award of the [[Indian Science Congress Association]] in 2010 and the BioSpectrum Person of the Year Award in 2011.<ref name="Biotech Park" /> In 2012, the [[Government of India]] awarded him the civilian honor of [[Padma Shri]].<ref name="Biotech Park" /><ref name="Padma Shri" /> He also holds the Fellowships of [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]], and [[Indian Society for Parasitology]].<ref name="INSA Profile" />
